## Review summary

The core deliverable — a shared `dispatch_core.py` flock-based concurrency gate replacing 3 previously independent/uncapped worker-spawn paths — is architecturally sound and verified under real multi-process contention (all 18 tests pass, including a genuine multi-OS-process race test). The 6 superseded scripts are renamed with history preserved, and behavior is faithfully carried forward into the 3 new scripts.

However, I reproduced a real, confirmed bug: `dispatch_core._upsert_wiring_row()` only calls `_ensure_wiring_registry_table()` (a no-op `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), never the new schema migration that widens the `wiring_registry` CHECK constraint to allow `'dispatch_event'`. Against a DB seeded with the actual pre-existing production schema, `record_dispatch_event()` throws a CHECK constraint violation on every call — silently swallowed by the best-effort exception handler. So the `dispatch_event` audit-trail rows this consolidation is supposed to produce will never actually get written in production, contradicting the commit's claim that the migration was "verified... idempotent." None of the 18 new tests catch it since they all build fresh DBs that already have the widened constraint baked in.

**Verdict: reject** (tier1 — recorded, not overridden). Wrote `review-verdict.json` with full detail and a suggested fix (call `init_db_silent()`/`_migrate_schema()` in the write path, plus a test seeded with the real pre-migration schema). No `.github/workflows/**` changes in this diff.
